TLDR: It's Mid.

Six hundred years of cryo-sleep just to wake up in a galaxy that looks like a Ubisoft executive’s fever dream. BioWare scraped the surface of Dragon Age Inquisition and decided the Andromeda galaxy needed more open-world slop. 

There are stints of good writing hidden under the rubble. The combat is fast and fluid, even if I prefer the tactical weight of the originals. The environments are beautiful, almost makes you forget you’re doing errands for NPCs with the personality of wet cardboard.

For a series that set the benchmark for the industry, being average is a failure to me. Some will tell you not to compare, but I prefer work that tries to be special rather than a game that copies bland trends and lets you turn your brain off for sixty hours of mainly busywork. 

Not a leap into the unknown, a crawl through hollowed-out memory lane. Skip it.

Good game on its own. It is worth the price (on sale). However, the graphics looks so bad sometimes. The mission design is boring, repetitive. The story's pacing is confusing. The final mission came sooner than I expected. Also, the final boss encounter needed a better ending.

Overall I am still recommending the game because of the combat system, new setting and possibly a new series of stories to unfold! I hope Bioware take their time and deliver a game like ME2.

So this game got a whooooole lot of hate when it came out.

By all accounts it was buggy, unfinished and rushed.

Well, it still feels sort of unfinished - nothing particular I can point to, just a general sense of 'this needs some polish' but it's not at all bad. The support NPC's are serviceable with a few really good moments (and one or two stand outs), the storyline's by-the-numbers but solid, the combat's sort of repetitive but not actually bad, the character development is... Uhm... Anyway, the usual Mass Effect problems are on full display - a lot of running around on tiny fetch quests when you'd think you'd have better things to do, a profound and inexplicable disconnect between the really rather excellent world-building and the actual game you end up playing (which yaws especially wide whenever there's a cutscene), some *extremely* stupid choices being made by the in-game characters and one or two fairly stupid ones which are foisted upon you but...

 Yeah, on the whole I enjoyed my time with it and I think it's a gentle shame that we probably won't see the sequel.

The graphics & the gameplay are good , but the slow pacing, the performance, narrative & removal of paragon/renegade options etc... are the game's weakest points (even with mods installed). I've tried to like it & view it as a different game from the original trilogy , but I cannot bring myself to continue... The original trilogy is too iconic for me to enjoy this game. Unfortunately , It feels like a chore every time I launch the game... The next entry seems to continue Sheperd's journey & I hope Bioware have learned from their recent mistakes & give us a proper game.

The Good: The main campaign is engaging and the galactic views are stunning. It’s the ultimate "low-stress" game for unwinding after a long day.
The Bad: Secondary missions lack variety and can feel like a chore, also some planets are just like a bit repetitive.
If you want a space-travel simulator to pair with your favorite podcasts or playlists, this is a must-play. Just manage your expectations regarding the side content.
